purpose: Real-publication mission-loop qualification; cases do not prescribe a tool sequence or scientific conclusion.
review_rule: A completed run is not a passed case. Review the saved answer against actual retrieved copies and assess correctness, trace fidelity, collaboration value and readability separately.

cases.question: Find the published REEACT trial abstract (PMID 26559241). What population and treatment comparison does it explicitly report? Give a short source-linked answer.
cases.scope: One focused fact question. Use the published abstract as valid evidence for what it says. Additional searches are useful only if the initial record is insufficient.
review_checks: Population and comparators match retrieved abstract
Exact source and model-call records are inspectable

cases.question: Find the published REEACT trial abstract (PMID 26559241). Does this abstract report the exact random-number seed used for allocation? Explain briefly and distinguish an unreported detail from evidence of flawed randomization.
cases.scope: The question is about what the abstract reports. Do not invent an allocation seed or treat missing reporting as demonstrated bias.
review_checks: Missing reporting distinguished from demonstrated bias

cases.question: What did the REEACT-2 randomized trial compare, and what does its published abstract say about telephone support for computerized cognitive behavioural therapy for depression? Find a relevant scholarly record and explain the comparison clearly.
cases.scope: Do not conflate REEACT-2 with REEACT. Cite the source actually inspected. Missing full text can prompt complementary searches but does not invalidate a published abstract.

cases.question: Find a randomized study in primary care that compared telephone-facilitated computerized therapy with less-supported computerized therapy for adult depression. What treatment contrast was tested? Use a source-linked explanation.
cases.scope: The trial acronym is not supplied. Revise the search if needed; do not substitute a psychotherapy study with a different treatment contrast without explaining that difference.
review_checks: No unsupported claim of comprehensive coverage

cases.question: Compare the REEACT and REEACT-2 trial evidence on computerized therapy and human support for adult depression. Obtain an independent peer check of whether the two trials tested the same comparison, then integrate the useful feedback into a readable answer.
cases.scope: Use real retrieved publications. Distinguish study identity, treatment comparison and follow-up. Preserve disagreement and explain whether peer feedback changed the answer.
review_checks: Independent peer contribution and exact reply present
Requester sees the reply in a later call
Revision or retained interpretation has source support

cases.question: A journal report and an HTA report may describe the same REEACT-2 trial. Find their relationship, ask a peer to check whether they are independent randomized samples, and summarize what can be concluded without double-counting participants.
cases.scope: Relevant identifiers include DOI 10.1192/bjp.bp.116.192435 and DOI 10.3310/hta20890. Treat these as leads to verify, not as proof of study identity.
review_checks: Peer challenge is visible separately from delivery acknowledgment

cases.question: Explain why the REEACT and REEACT-2 findings should not be read as a simple contradiction about digital therapy. Search trial reports, relevant corrections and participant-experience evidence; collaborate to distinguish observed results from possible explanations.
cases.scope: An accessible abstract is useful evidence. Seek complementary information when methods or engagement detail is missing. Do not assume a correction changes outcomes before inspecting it, or infer an individual causal mechanism from group results.
review_checks: Parallel work and dependent integration both observable
Report separates findings from proposed explanations

cases.question: Use the REEACT-2 abstract plus any useful accessible companion report to explain whether additional support improved the reported outcome. Ask an independent peer to check the population, comparison and follow-up behind the conclusion. Give a useful answer even if a full-text route is unavailable.
cases.scope: Try a complementary scholarly or publisher route when a detail is missing. Keep an inaccessible article distinct from a negative scientific result; preserve usable retrieved evidence and identify any remaining detail briefly downstream.
review_checks: Missing detail leads to an alternative inquiry
No global stop on optional unavailable full text
Peer evidence consumed rather than merely delivered

cases.question: Prepare a research brief on computerized cognitive behavioural therapy for adult depression in primary care using REEACT, REEACT-2 and relevant participant-experience evidence. Compare what was actually tested, develop two distinguishable explanations for engagement or outcome differences, and propose a focused next research question. Have peers check key evidence and revise the brief where warranted.
cases.scope: Breadth should serve the question. Separate observed trial findings, methodological uncertainty, hypotheses and proposed next work. Use concise clear prose, explain technical terms and keep run metadata outside the research brief.
cases.followup: Narrow the next research question to the contribution of human support. Preserve the previous report and source counts, and revise only the affected interpretation and proposed study comparison.
review_checks: Report is understandable without trace metadata

cases.question: Investigate whether differences in support or engagement could help explain the REEACT and REEACT-2 findings. Find and compare relevant real publications, invite an independent challenge, preserve useful partial results and continue with accepted evidence after peer feedback.
cases.scope: This case also checks durable execution across a separately controlled host interruption. The interruption is a test action, not a reason to invent a limitation in the scientific answer. Preserve exact selected model, sources, messages and prior outputs.
cases.followup: Review the latest saved answer against the earlier peer challenge. Explain what changed, what remained supported and the most useful unresolved research question.
review_checks: Uncertain effects distinguished from known results
Unchanged selected model and tool settings
Useful scientific continuation visible after recovery
